sitekit

Why it exists

A generated site that cannot say where each sentence came from will eventually say something nobody wrote. The second generator was about to ship that.

How it works

Sections are a closed union, checked before render. One set of React renderers draws them. Every field can carry where it came from, so a page can show that a line was supplied rather than invented.

Where it fits

Loki can stand up a site because the site is data. sitekit is that data. design-tokens is what it looks like. bip-kit is the long writing inside it.

Read the package documentation

A website as data.

A site is pages; a page is sections; sections come from a closed union of shapes validated by Zod at runtime. One set of React renderers draws every site. A provenance sidecar records where every generated field came from — so "we fabricated nothing" is an assertion, not a promise.

Extracted from substrata's hosted-site model (2026-08). Decided in orangecat's ADR-0003 (the Site Factory).

Why a closed union

A generator emitting data against this schema is a task with a machine-checkable result; a generator emitting components is not. Per-site quality becomes a property of the renderers — fixing the cards renderer improves every site ever generated. And the schema is where review happens: validateSite() returns path: message errors a model can act on directly.

The current kinds: hero (with optional CTAs), prose, stats, meter, cards, definitions, feature (a figure beside a story), contact (locations, address, hours — the fields provenance exists to protect), faq, index, table. Most kinds take an optional anchor, and the schema rejects any index entry or hero action that points at a fragment nothing carries. Extending the union is a deliberate act in THIS repo — a new kind lands with its schema, its renderer, and its tests in one commit, and every consumer gets it on the next version bump.

Install

pnpm add @bitbaum/sitekit

ESM-only. react >= 18 is a peer dependency of @bitbaum/sitekit/react; the root export is framework-free (a Node generator or CI check can use it without React).

Use

import { validateSite, siteNavItems, sitePageAt, pageRendersOwnHeader } from '@bitbaum/sitekit';

const result = validateSite(generatorOutput);
if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('\n'));
const site = result.data; // fully typed SiteSpec from here on
import Link from 'next/link';
import { SiteMasthead, SiteFooter, SiteSections } from '@bitbaum/sitekit/react';

<SiteMasthead chrome={site.chrome} navItems={siteNavItems(site.pages)} currentPath={path} Link={Link} />
<SiteSections sections={page.sections} />
<SiteFooter chrome={site.chrome} />

Link is the one framework seam: it defaults to a plain <a>, which is correct everywhere; a Next.js app passes next/link to get client-side navigation back.

Application shell

Product apps use the same masthead, navigation and footer with the application appearance. Import @bitbaum/sitekit/styles.css once. No Tailwind setup is required for this appearance; --sk-* variables map it to the product's shared design tokens. Existing document sites keep their utility-class appearance.

<SiteMasthead appearance="application" chrome={chrome} navItems={nav}
  currentPath="analyze" mainId="main-content" Link={Link}
  brand={<Brand />} actions={<AccountControl />} />
<SiteFooter appearance="application" chrome={chrome} Link={Link}
  links={[{ href: '/roadmap', label: 'Roadmap' }]} extra="Beta" />

The package owns the responsive menu, its native no-JavaScript fallback, Escape/outside/route dismissal, skip link, active states, touch targets and footer layout. Products supply labels, navigation data, identity and account slots. Fix shared chrome here, then release and update consumers through their normal dependency checks and deployment pipeline.

Provenance — the check behind "fabricate no facts"

A closed schema invites completion: a model handed a stats section wants numbers in it. So absence is first-class and typed. The generator emits a sidecar keyed by JSON path:

import { assertDeliverable, notFoundPaths } from '@bitbaum/sitekit';

const provenance = {
  'chrome.name':                    { kind: 'scraped', url: 'https://cafe-beispiel.ch/' },
  'pages.0.sections.1.paragraphs.0':{ kind: 'operator' },   // a human typed it
  'pages.0.sections.4.cards.0.meta':{ kind: 'inferred' },   // a model invented it
  'pages.0.sections.7.rows.0.1':    { kind: 'not-found' },  // we looked; it isn't public
};

assertDeliverable(provenance); // throws: names the inferred path
notFoundPaths(provenance);     // the honest gaps — in a pitch, these ARE the pitch

not-found is the difference between unknown and empty: it records that the looking happened, which is what makes "here is what we could not find out about you" an honest sentence instead of an excuse.

The styling contract

The renderers emit semantic utility classes and nothing else — no colours, faces, or radii ship in this package. Each consumer defines the tokens, which is how fifty sites share one renderer without looking like one company. (Uniform everywhere except aesthetics. Do NOT point consumers at @fleet/design-tokens values — those make things look like the fleet; inherit the shape, choose your own values.)

Classes the renderers use, to be defined by the consumer's Tailwind theme:

GroupClasses
Text`text-fg-primary` `text-fg-secondary` `text-fg-tertiary` `text-fg-muted`
Surfaces`bg-surface-page` `bg-surface-raised`
Borders`border-subtle` `border-strong` `divide-subtle`
Accent & status`bg-accent` `decoration-accent` `bg-status-positive` `bg-status-warning` `bg-status-negative`
Type`font-heading` `font-mono` `tracking-caps` `tracking-display`
Layout`max-w-shell` `max-w-prose` `scrollbar-hide`

With Tailwind 4, define them as @theme variables (--color-fg-primary, --font-heading, …) and add the package to content scanning:

@import 'tailwindcss';
@source '../node_modules/@bitbaum/sitekit/dist';

Substrata's app/globals.css is the reference implementation of the contract.

Not in this package

  • No design tokens. See above — that is the point.
  • No scraper. siteFromUrl() (extraction from a live site, with

provenance) is the planned next module; the schema is its target.

  • No HTTP, no framework. Same rule as every package in this fleet.

Verify

pnpm run verify  # lint + typecheck + build + test — same command CI runs

Tests import the package by name (@bitbaum/sitekit, @bitbaum/sitekit/react), so a broken exports map fails in CI, not at the first consumer.

Part of bitbaum — AI-native products on open infrastructure, built in Zürich. Every package here lists the apps that use it: which apps use sitekit.

Application footers can pass groups: [{ label, links: [{ href, label }] }] for semantic navigation groups. Existing flat links remain supported. Consumers can configure --sk-header-height, --sk-mobile-header-height, --sk-display-weight, --sk-display-leading, --sk-display-tracking and --sk-footer-gap through their theme adapter, without replacing shared markup.
